ac: AC-2 (spec section 5 'AC-2 (plan review P-4)', plan section 7 P-4 option a)
title: P-4 eager wipe is not implemented: a used refresh token stays in the shadowed store after the abort / 401 path when the guard did not clear
evidence: spec.md section 5 records: 'when the token is marked used and the guard did not clear, any other store still holding that token is wiped at once, so no stale copy outlives the 16-entry record'. plan-review.md P-4 is marked 'Resolved (option a)' and plan.md P-4 promises a test 'in the R2-3 repro the sessionStorage copy is gone right after the 120 s abort'. `failedRefresh` (api-client.ts:147-164) only calls `clearSession()` when `isSamePostedSession` is true; otherwise it re-reads and throws or returns without calling `clearSessionHoldingRefresh`. Executed: R2-3 shape (u-1/r1 in sessionStorage, u-2 written to localStorage at 60 s, abort at 121 s) -> `sessionStorage.ef_refresh === 'r1'` right after `A:AUTH_REQUIRED`; same on the 401 path (`controlled()` + answer 401 while u-2 stored) -> 'r1' still present; same on the AC-3 reuse path (u-1/r9 in local, abort) -> session copy 'r1' still present. The existing ac2 test only checks the copy after the NEXT request (lazy wipe in doRefresh), not 'right after the abort'. The exploit from P-4 (17 marks evict r1, then re-POST) did NOT reproduce: after 16 successful u-2 rotations `setSession` wiped the other store at the first rotation and `posts` still contained r1 once; a same-posted failure calls `clearSession()` which wipes both stores. So the stale copy can only outlive 16 marks if all 16 are non-clearing race outcomes (other tab rotated / other user stored during this tab's POST). Impact today: a consumed refresh token lingers in sessionStorage until the next refresh attempt; UX for R2-S1 shows a signed-in user whose refresh is dead until the next 401.
fix: Either implement option (a): in `failedRefresh`, when `isSamePostedSession` is false, call `clearSessionHoldingRefresh(cur.refreshToken)` before the step-2 re-read (the helper already applies the P-3 'bump only if active store' rule and never touches a store holding another token), and add the planned assertion to the R2-3 / X-4 tests; or pick option (b) explicitly: delete the section-5 line and record the eviction residual, and change plan-review P-4 from 'Resolved (option a)' to (b).

title: A lock result of '' (empty string) passes the AC-5 check and apiFetch retries the original request WITHOUT a bearer, returning a raw 401
evidence: `withRefreshLock` guards with `typeof token !== 'string'`; an empty string is a string, so '' is returned as the access token. `withBearer(base, '')` (api-client.ts:353-358) treats a falsy token as 'no bearer' and deletes `Authorization`, so the retry at line 392 is sent unauthenticated and the raw 401 `Response` is returned to the caller. Executed with `installLocks({ request: () => Promise.resolve('') })`: outcome `A:401`, bearers `["Bearer old", null]`. Spec AC-5 wording ('no string token') is satisfied literally, but its goal ('does not retry the original request without a bearer') is not. Same premise as X-S2 (a LockManager that resolves without running the callback); `doRefresh` itself can never return '' because `readStore` requires a truthy access token, so this needs a non-conforming lock manager.
fix: api-client.ts:295: `if (typeof token !== 'string' || !token) throw networkError();` and add '' to the AC-5 it.each in ac4-ac5-no-bearerless-send.test.ts.

title: Values that look relative but are cross-origin pass safeRedirect: '//evil.example/x', '\\evil.example/x', '/\evil.example/x', 'https:evil.example', 'https://evil.example\@pay.test'
evidence: `safeRedirect` keeps `raw` whenever `new URL(raw, origin).protocol` is http(s). WHATWG parsing turns scheme-relative and backslash-relative inputs into `http(s)://evil.example/...`. Executed: all five values are returned unchanged and `new URL(redirectUrl, origin).host === 'evil.example'`; `payment-handoff-view.tsx:68` then assigns `window.location.href`. The spec only requires rejecting non-http(s) schemes and defers the host allow-list to the server (S-4 server part), so this is a documented residual rather than a spec breach; recorded because the spec text 'relative URL ... kept unchanged' reads as same-origin while these are not. Control-character and whitespace scheme tricks (\u0000javascript:, 'javascript\t:', JAVASCRIPT://%0a, ws:, ftp:, mailto:, about:blank, 'javascript:') are all rejected correctly.
fix: Cheap client-side tightening without a host list: treat as relative only when `raw.startsWith('/') && !/^[\/\\]{2}/.test(raw)`; treat as absolute only when `/^https?:\/\//i.test(raw)` and the parsed `href` round-trips (`new URL(raw).href` starts with the same scheme+host without backslashes); otherwise fallback. Or keep as is and add these shapes to the S-4 server-part deferral note so the backend allow-list owner knows the client passes them through.

title: A throwing Storage.getItem on localStorage now hides a valid sessionStorage session (regression vs c5fb598)
evidence: `readStore` returns `{ kind: 'invalid' }` from its catch block, and `activeStore` stops at the first non-absent store. Before this change `readFrom` returned null on a throw and `peekSession` fell through to sessionStorage. P-6 defines 'present' as both `ef_token` and `ef_user` existing; a storage read that throws is not 'present'. Executed: valid u-1 session in sessionStorage, `Storage.prototype.getItem` throws only for `localStorage.getItem('ef_token')` -> `peekSession()` is null (expected 'u-1'). Rare path (per-key storage exceptions from privacy extensions / quota probes), `store()` already handles the accessor-level throw.
fix: In `readStore`, wrap only the two `getItem` reads in a try/catch that returns `{ kind: 'absent' }`, and keep `{ kind: 'invalid' }` for JSON/shape/role failures of a store that is present.

title: Fallback path (no showModal): Escape only works while focus is inside the dialog; no focus trap or inert background
evidence: In the `else` branch the component sets the `open` attribute and listens for `keydown` on the dialog element itself, so a keydown whose target is outside the dialog (focus on body after a click on the backdrop/elsewhere) never reaches the handler. Executed in jsdom (which has no showModal): open the dialog, blur the focused button so `document.activeElement === document.body`, `fireEvent.keyDown(document.body, { key: 'Escape' })` -> dialog still open (0 DELETE, so no safety issue). The native path (`showModal`, used by every current browser) gets Esc through the `cancel` event regardless of focus, so this affects only the fallback. The fallback also does not trap Tab or mark the page `inert`, so keyboard users in that branch can reach the page behind the modal while `aria-modal='true'` claims otherwise.
fix: In the fallback branch attach the Escape `keydown` listener to `document` (remove it in the cleanup) and, optionally, a minimal Tab-wrap between the two buttons; or document that the fallback is a test-only path.

title: No mutation-test record (M-1..M-18, W-1, W-2) and the planned Google X-15 test is missing
evidence: plan.md section 6 sets a threshold of 18/18 (WP-A) and 5/5 (WP-B) mutations that must each fail at least one new test. gate-report.json and docs/workflow/frontend-debt-r5/gate/ contain lint/typecheck/build/test/e2e/go/audit/sast/secrets/tamper logs only; no mutation ids appear anywhere in the folder except plan.md / plan-review.md. Plan P-8 also promised a test for the Google edge (google 200, devices 200, refresh 200 bad body -> restored session works until a 401, then AUTH_REQUIRED with 1 POST); ac2-used-refresh.test.ts only has a seeded-session variant. I executed the Google scenario myself (c5-google.test.ts: loginWithGoogle with refresh 200 'junk' and with 401; devices 503 variant) and it behaves as specified (posts ['rG'], session and ef_refresh cleared at the end), so this is a records/test gap, not a defect. Not a code finding, hence 'suspicion'.
repro:
grep -rl -i mutation docs/workflow/frontend-debt-r5/  # only plan.md, plan-review.md, tier.json, findings-review.json
node -e "const g=require('./docs/workflow/frontend-debt-r5/gate-report.json'); console.log(JSON.stringify(g).match(/\\b(M-1[0-8]|M-[1-9]|W-[12])\\b/g))"  # null
fix: Run the plan section 6 mutation set (or a documented subset) and record the per-mutation failing test in gate-report.json or a mutation.md; add the P-8 Google test (my c5 repro can be reused as is).

title: Chrome close-watcher can force-close the native dialog while the DELETE is in flight; React keeps it 'open' until the DELETE settles
evidence: Chromium's close-watcher anti-abuse rule lets `cancel.preventDefault()` block Esc only once per user activation; a second Esc skips `cancel` and fires `close` directly. `onClose` -> `dismiss()` -> ignored while busy, so the native element closes (hidden, focus returns to the page) while `confirmOpen` stays true and the trigger/primary/tier controls remain disabled until the DELETE settles, after which `setConfirmOpen(false)` unmounts it. No second DELETE is possible (confirm is disabled and `cancellingRef` guards). Not executable in jsdom; the unit test 'a close the browser does on its own syncs state through onDismiss' covers the non-busy case only.
repro: Not executed (requires a real Chromium close-watcher). Manual: open the dialog, click 'Huỷ giữ vé' with a slow DELETE (throttle), press Esc twice quickly without clicking; observe the dialog vanish while the spinner state persists in React until the response.
fix: In `onClose`, when busy, re-open with `showModal()` on the next frame (if the element is still connected), or accept and document that the dialog may be hidden while the request completes.
